org.apache.lucene.internal.vectorization.reason: Stable Rust has no portable SIMD (std::simd is nightly-only), so the jdk.incubator.vector lane kernels cannot be reproduced. PanamaVectorConstants::PREFERRED_VECTOR_BITSIZE is zero, every lane guard fails, and the whole computation runs Lucene's own scalar tail through DefaultVectorUtilSupport. The divergence is declared in src/internal/vectorization/panama_vector_util_support.rs.

org.apache.lucene.analysis.standard.Stan.reason: Lucene's scanner is generated by JFlex from StandardTokenizerImpl.jflex; these members are the generated packed tables and the JFlex reader protocol that drives them. This port applies the same UAX #29 rules through the unicode-segmentation crate instead of transcribing a generated automaton. Declared on the type in src/analysis/standard.rs and in specs/modules/standard-tokenizer-strategy.md.

org.apache.lucene.analysis.AbstractAnaly.reason: getPattern returns a java.util.regex.Pattern. The crate has no regular-expression engine of that kind (util::automaton::RegExp implements Lucene's own regexp syntax over an automaton, not Java's), so porting it means adopting a new dependency. CLAUDE.md 13.3 requires the user's approval before adopting a dependency, so this one member is held open pending that decision rather than resolved unilaterally.

org.apache.lucene.document.LatLonPoint.reason: The five query factories (newBoxQuery, newBoxInternal, newDistanceQuery, newPolygonQuery, newGeometryQuery, makeContainsGeometryQuery, newDistanceFeatureQuery) each return a Query. None of the geo query types they build — LatLonPointQuery, LatLonPointDistanceQuery, LatLonPointDistanceFeatureQuery — implements the search::Query trait yet: they exist as standalone types carrying their own visitors and bounds. Wiring them into the search API (create_weight, to_query_string, visit, query_eq, query_hash, and SpatialQuery::getScorerSupplier) is the work these factories depend on, and is tracked as its own gap rather than hidden inside this one.
